 Borrowers around the country are turning to private lenders to help pay for college since the Trump administration imposed new limits on federal student loans. Changes that took effect this fall for the federal loan program include caps on loans for particular programs as well as limits on the amount parents can borrow to pay for their children’s schooling. Generally, loans from the federal government offer more flexible repayment terms, the possibility of forgiveness after 10 years in public service, and often have lower interest rates.

 NEW YORK — New limits on federal student loans filled Chloe Frabotta with anxiety as she began studying in New York City to become a physician assistant.
 The changes that took effect this fall include caps on loans for particular programs as well as limits on the amount parents can borrow to pay for their children’s schooling. Up until weeks before Frabotta, 25, started her program, it was up in the air whether it would count as a “professional” program with higher loan limits.
